newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian coalition to meet on oil prices July 8 - PTI.
newsitem.headline: Indian coalition to meet on oil prices July 8 - PTI.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition will consider raising domestic oil prices to plug a mounting subsidy bill at a meeting set for July 8, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Thursday.

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's 15-party alliance had been scheduled to meet on Friday to discuss oil prices. The news agency said a crisis in Gujral's Janata Dal party forced the coalition to postpone the meeting.
It would be the third time that the centre-left coalition, deeply split over the issue, has put off the crucial meeting.
The government owes state oil companies an estimated 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) and the companies have complained they cannot keep importing crude unless domestic prices are raised.

The communists are vigorously opposed to any price increase, while Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram have argued for moderate rises in the prices of some petroleum products coupled with the eventual dismantling of state controls.
The Communist Party of India (Marxist) wants customs and excise duties on oil eliminated and has submitted an alternative plan to avoid higher petroleum prices, which it says would hurt the poor.
